record.title: Google DeepMind preprint extends Boyd-family records across high polynomial degrees
record.summary: A Google DeepMind preprint presents a five-parameter extension of Boyd's construction for small Mahler-measure polynomials. The authors report verified irreducible examples below Boyd's limit point at all 995 even degrees they evaluate from 12 to 2000, including six improvements over published values. This advances finite-degree records but does not settle Lehmer's conjecture or prove every listed polynomial globally minimal; the reported results have not been independently reproduced in this review.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors introduce a five-parameter Generalized Boyd construction and report irreducible polynomials with Mahler measure below Boyd's limit point α1 for every even degree they evaluate from 12 through 2000 (995 degrees).

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Across the evaluated set, the authors report that their construction attains 991 of 995 best-known records and improves six previously published values; this is a finite benchmark result and does not establish global minimality at each degree.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The paper describes an interactive human–AI workflow combining Gemini, numerical search, distributed compute and exact symbolic verification to identify patterns that informed the generalized construction.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED_LIMITATION
claims.text: The paper does not prove or disprove Lehmer's conjecture; the evaluated dataset is finite, and this review did not independently reproduce the construction or reported values.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The linked arXiv ancillary CSV is directly downloadable and contains 996 degree rows, from degree 10 through 2000; this review checked file availability and row structure but did not recalculate the entries.

evidence_gaps.description: The construction, dataset and six reported improvements were not independently reproduced in this review.
The benchmark reports best-known values over evaluated methods and a finite range; it does not prove that every listed polynomial is globally minimal for its degree or resolve Lehmer's conjecture.

brief.importance_rationale: If the reported construction and finite-degree values are correct, they extend a longstanding family of low Mahler-measure records across high even degrees and illustrate a potentially reusable route from large computational searches to analytical structure. The importance is notable within mathematics and AI-assisted discovery, but the preprint does not solve Lehmer's conjecture and has not been independently reproduced here.
limitations: This is a single author-reported preprint; no independent mathematical reproduction was performed in this review.
The reported 995-degree benchmark is finite and does not prove global minimality for every degree or solve Lehmer's conjecture.
The paper's AI workflow attribution and aggregate computational search are described by the authors; independent mechanism-level attribution is not established.
The review did not independently recompute the accessible ancillary CSV or rerun supplementary code.

The authors report verified irreducible examples below Boyd's limit point at all 995 even degrees they evaluate from 12 to 2000, including six improvements over published values. This advances finite-degree records but does not settle Lehmer's conjecture or prove every listed polynomial globally minimal; the reported results have not been independently reproduced in this review.

technical.claimed_result: Authors report a five-parameter Generalized Boyd family that produces irreducible examples below α1 for all evaluated even degrees 12–2000, holds 991/995 best-known records in that finite set and improves six previously published values.
technical.demonstrated_result: The arXiv v1 paper and described exact-verification methods are publicly inspectable. The linked ancillary CSV is accessible and contains 996 degree rows from 10 through 2000; its mathematical entries were not independently checked.
technical.mechanism: The paper describes large-scale numerical search with reinforcement learning, evolutionary and priority search, followed by cyclotomic factor analysis of recurring coefficient structure. The authors derive a five-parameter family intended to avoid degree gaps in Boyd's one-parameter specializations; individual polynomial irreducibility is checked symbolically over the rationals.
technical.regime: Author-reported evaluation across even polynomial degrees 10–2000, with the generalized family evaluated at 995 degrees from 12 through 2000. Comparisons include published best-known values through degree 250 and results from the paper's search methods.
technical.reproducibility: The linked arXiv ancillary CSV was directly retrieved and inspected for headers, 996 rows and degree coverage from 10 through 2000. This establishes artifact availability and row structure only; no entries, irreducibility tests, Mahler measures or reported literature improvements were independently recalculated in this activation.
technical.strongest_baseline: Prior published Mahler-measure records for the covered degrees and the one-parameter Boyd family; the paper reports six strict improvements over previous published values.

brief.title: Google DeepMind preprint extends Boyd-family records across high polynomial degrees
brief.why_it_matters: Lehmer's problem links number theory with entropy and growth rates in several mathematical fields. Extending explicit constructions across high degrees can improve the finite record map and offers a worked case where computational search and exact symbolic checks feed into a compact analytical family. Independent mathematical review is still needed, and this result is not a solution to the conjecture.
